clue.text: Enjoys hot dish

parts.note: to enjoy something is to have it, as in 'enjoys good health'
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone who likes a spicy meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Hash is a dish of chopped meat and potato fried together, so it is a type of dish.

clue.text: Era in which Oriental individual embraces church

parts.note: E stands for East, so Oriental gives E

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold inside, so the word for individual wraps around the church letters

parts.note: one means a single individual
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A historical period when an Eastern person took up a church.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eocene is a geological epoch, loosely an era, of the Tertiary period about 56 to 34 million years ago.

clue.text: Soldiers in disgrace or laudable exploit

indicators.note: in places the soldiers inside the word for disgrace

parts.note: attaint is an archaic word for a stain or disgrace
men is a common word for soldiers, the ranks

explanation.surface: A choice between troops being shamed or doing something praiseworthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disgrace' here is the archaic noun attaint, a stain on one's honour, not the modern verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An attainment is an achievement, something accomplished that deserves praise.

clue.text: Stand-in showing twice the spirit?

definitions.meaning: a lookalike who takes an actor's place in a scene
a bar order of two measures of whisky or gin, with a hint at a ghostly lookalike

explanation.surface: An understudy who has double the enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: A double is both a body double who stands in for an actor and a two-measure serving of spirits.

clue.text: One carpet under pound? It's free!

indicators.note: in a down answer the pieces for one and carpet sit below the pound letter

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound sterling, from libra
the Roman numeral I is one
to carpet someone is to scold them, to berate

explanation.surface: A rug selling for under a pound sounds like it is being given away.
explanation.definitionFit: To liberate is to set free, a verb matching free used as a verb.

clue.text: Unemployed daughter visits French island

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside, so the daughter letter enters the French word for island

parts.note: île is French for island
D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A jobless daughter goes on holiday to a French island.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle describes someone out of work, without a job to occupy them.

clue.text: Young bird settling snugly

definitions.meaning: a chick too young to leave its nest
curling up cosily against something, as a child does against a parent

explanation.surface: A chick tucking itself comfortably into place.
explanation.definitionFit: A nestling is a chick still in the nest, and nestling is also the participle of to nestle, settling cosily.

clue.text: Muslim ruler wants Ancient Mariner's tale written up

indicators.note: in a down clue, written upwards means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Coleridge's poem is The Rime of the Ancient Mariner, so the tale is a rime

explanation.surface: A sheikh would like a version of Coleridge's sea poem.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir is a title for a Muslim prince, commander or governor.

clue.text: Stronghold with excellent fencing or one with better grounds

indicators.note: to fence is to enclose, so the excellent letters surround the stronghold

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written with the digit as the letter I
a fort is a fortified stronghold
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A fort surrounded by a fine fence, or one with better land around it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grounds' suggests land around a castle, but here means reasons: the Latin phrase argues from a stronger case.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortiori is Latin for 'from the stronger', used of an argument that holds with even more reason.

clue.text: King had this made afresh with Republican input

indicators.note: the Republican letter is put into the remade letters
made afresh means remade, so the letters of made are rearranged

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican in US politics

explanation.surface: A monarch remade something with help from a Republican.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King' looks like a monarch, but it is Martin Luther King, whose 1963 speech began 'I have a dream'.
explanation.definitionFit: Martin Luther King's most famous speech declared he had a vision of equality.

clue.text: Animal in elevated position heard female

indicators.note: heard means the word for being up high is said aloud and spelt another way

parts.note: something in an elevated position is high up
Ena is a girl's name, a crossword standby for a female

explanation.surface: An animal perched up high listened to a female.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyena is a doglike African and Asian carnivore known for its laughing call.

clue.text: Royal servant's third little piggy?

definitions.meaning: a Yeoman Warder of the Tower of London, the possessive making it 'Royal servant is'
in the nursery rhyme This Little Piggy, the third piggy had roast beef

explanation.surface: A footman in the palace is the one from the nursery rhyme.
explanation.walkthrough: BEEFEATER is the nickname for a Yeoman Warder at the Tower of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Beefeaters are the ceremonial guards at the Tower, and a beef eater is what the third pig in the rhyme was.

clue.text: Remove sin from learner Seneca corrupted

indicators.note: corrupted text is jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A student cleaning away a philosopher's moral corruption.
explanation.walkthrough: Seneca was a Roman Stoic philosopher.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleanse someone is to purify them, washing away their sins.

clue.text: Damage follows cold spell

indicators.note: the damage word comes after the cold letter

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
to damage is to harm

explanation.surface: Harm comes after a period of cold weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spell' looks like a stretch of weather, but means a magic incantation.
explanation.definitionFit: A charm is a magic spell or incantation.

clue.text: Grow weak after the first severe pain

indicators.note: the letters that come after the first one are used, so its opening letter goes

parts.note: to languish is to lose strength or vigour

explanation.surface: Someone fading after a first bout of serious pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Anguish is severe mental or physical suffering.

clue.text: Super-soft one getting tickled?

parts.note: grand means splendid, super
piano is the musical term for soft

explanation.surface: Someone very gentle who enjoys being tickled.
explanation.walkthrough: Pianists are said to tickle the ivories, so the tickled one is the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing the piano is jokingly called tickling the ivories, so the instrument is what gets tickled.

clue.text: Horrible death not exactly cherished

indicators.note: something horrible is a mess, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A dreadful death for someone not much loved.
explanation.definitionFit: Being loathed is an ironic understatement for falling short of being cherished.

clue.text: Perhaps bitter about performing solo

indicators.note: about means around, so the ale wraps the performing word

parts.note: bitter is a kind of ale, hence perhaps
an act that is on is performing

explanation.surface: A beer drinker on a solo turn, or a lone pint during a show.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is a British beer, a type of ale.
explanation.definitionFit: Alone means by oneself, as a solo performer is.

clue.text: Repeated phrase, from Taoist, on Reformation?

indicators.note: reformation is reshaping, so these letters are formed anew

explanation.surface: A question of whether a recurring saying comes from Taoist thought after a religious reform.
explanation.definitionFit: An ostinato is a musical motif repeated persistently throughout a piece.

clue.text: Diamonds set evenly in circlet

indicators.note: evenly means the even-numbered letters are picked: second, fourth, sixth

explanation.surface: Diamonds set at regular intervals around a ring or crown.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice is slang for diamonds, from their clear glittering look.

clue.text: Not being straight in dreadful court

parts.note: dire means dreadful

explanation.surface: Someone lying while in a terrible court case.
explanation.definitionFit: Indirect means not going straight, roundabout, as a route or answer.

clue.text: Gangster's existential anxiety

indicators.note: existential is read as 'existing in': the dread exists inside the mobster's word

explanation.surface: A mobster suffers from dread about life's meaning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Existential anxiety' looks like the whole definition, but 'existential' is the signal that the answer exists within the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A German loan word for deep dread or fear, often about the human condition.

clue.text: Damaging allegations about gallery took new form

indicators.note: about means around, so the mud wraps the gallery

parts.note: mud is slander, as in mudslinging
the Tate is the London art gallery

explanation.surface: Scandal around an art gallery changed it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutated means changed form, past tense to match took.

clue.text: Worked out as French duke in action

indicators.note: in places the French duke inside the action word

parts.note: a deed is an action
duc is French for duke

explanation.surface: Something figured out about a French nobleman doing something.
explanation.definitionFit: Deduced means reasoned out from evidence, a past tense like worked out.

clue.text: Murder mother for the estate?

indicators.note: for reads as standing in for the gap: the mother word slots between the two parts of the murder phrase

parts.note: to do in is slang for to kill
ma is mother

explanation.surface: Killing a parent to inherit the property.
explanation.definitionFit: A domain is lands held by a lord, an estate.

clue.text: Someone's skin fool keeps in cupboard

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the fool wraps the skin letters

parts.note: a clot is a fool
the skin of the word someone is its outer letters, S and E

explanation.surface: A fool stores someone's skin in a cupboard, a gruesome picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A closet is a small room or tall cupboard for storage.

clue.text: Star, confined, gaining little weight

indicators.note: gaining means adding, the weight comes after

parts.note: pent means shut in, as in pent-up
a gram is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: A celebrity locked away puts on a few grams.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentagram is a five-pointed star shape.

clue.text: Money taken from chapel funds

indicators.note: the letters are taken from within the words

explanation.surface: Cash removed from a church's collection.
explanation.definitionFit: Pelf is a contemptuous word for money, especially ill-gotten.

clue.text: Laos in rebellion too?

indicators.note: a rebellion is an uprising, upsetting order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Is the Asian country rising up as well?
explanation.definitionFit: Also means as well, a synonym of too.

clue.text: Home and Away is diversion going to pot

parts.note: being in means being at home
off means away, as in off on holiday

explanation.surface: Seems to be about TV soaps Home and Away and a distraction going wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Home and Away is an Australian soap; 'pot' is the snooker term for pocketing a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: An in-off in snooker is a ball deflected off another into a pocket.

clue.text: Armada almost making escape

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is left off

parts.note: an armada is a fleet of warships

explanation.surface: The Spanish fleet nearly getting away.
explanation.definitionFit: To flee is to run away, a verb like escape.

clue.text: Flower for all to see among many

indicators.note: among puts the certificate letter inside the many word

parts.note: lots means many
U is the universal film certificate, viewable by all

explanation.surface: A bloom on show for everyone among a crowd of others.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is a water lily, a flower sacred in Asian religions.

clue.text: Customers given two keys allowed man back inside

indicators.note: inside puts the turned-round words between the two keys

parts.note: C and E are musical keys

indicators.note: back means the words for allowed and man are read backwards

parts.note: let means allowed
Neil is a man's name

explanation.surface: Shoppers given two keys and a man let back in.
explanation.definitionFit: Clientele means the body of clients, a shop's customers collectively.
